epic.intent: Build full FWG world interaction: grounded generated characters and peoples, campaign memory and beliefs, political intrigue and diplomacy, actionable quests/events, and validated fantasy/world-mutation actions. Learn from static inspection of the downloaded AI Influence v6.0.2 DLL and packaged guide; independently implement the design in MNBL with explicit Bannerlord API adapters, without requiring AI Influence. Retain FWG source identity rather than treating presentation cultures as lore. Finish with real local inference evaluations comparing strong tool-using parent models and their SamsungLabs LittleBit-compressed derivatives. Select by measured end-to-end tool reliability under the target machine budget, not parameter count or perplexity alone. This epic is planning/backlog only; model runs and gameplay implementation are future ticket work.

successCriteria.text: Artifact-pinned AI Influence research identifies observed dialogue/action/diplomacy/API routes, design lessons, obfuscation limits and explicitly separate runtime unknowns; target code is not copied into the product.
AI context preserves FWG civilization, source UIDs, generated history, current campaign facts and NPC knowledge boundaries; no mandatory Calradia lore or fixed six-culture assumptions.
Persistent characters, dialogue, beliefs/rumours, NPC initiative and multi-step political intrigue produce observable, validated campaign effects with an auditable event/action history.

Typed tools cover negotiated political/economic actions, generated-world travel and quests, and a real supported FWG magic mutation; unauthorized, stale, cross-campaign and duplicate actions cannot corrupt state.

Inference is asynchronous and bounded; cancellation, failures, invalid output and unavailable models leave a playable campaign. Saves restore memory and action state consistently across rollback, cold restart, A/B worlds and two campaigns of one world.

A frozen held-out FWG tool-use suite ranks at least three feasible instruction/tool-capable parent candidates, evaluates LittleBit derivatives of at least two candidates at multiple documented compression settings, and reports paired reliability, latency, RAM/VRAM and storage results with exact artifacts and reproducible commands. Infeasible candidates are reported, not silently substituted with ordinary quantization.

The selected LittleBit checkpoint runs locally with Bannerlord on the target machine and passes final dialogue→intrigue→world-action→save/load acceptance. A no-go result leaves the epic unaccepted rather than claiming an unmeasured model winner.

epic.title: FWG living-world AI: characters, intrigue, world actions and LittleBit model evaluations

tickets.title: Freeze AI Influence code evidence and Bannerlord political hook map

acceptanceCriteria.text: Enumerate initial implemented tools and exact observable effects; world-changing requests cannot succeed only as dialogue.
Define measurable latency, concurrent NPC, memory and tool-success budgets before evaluation, tied to target hardware; distinguish prototype from release gates.
Describe AI/vanilla diplomacy ownership and disable/uninstall behavior without assuming Calradia or overwriting FWGC++ source.

tickets.body: Specify dialogue, beliefs, political intrigue, diplomacy/economy, travel/quests and supported magic/world effects. Define action ownership, information visibility, faction authority, commitments, consequences and capability discovery. Choose integrated behavior or explicit module bridge after inspecting internal FWG seams; preserve existing campaigns and active map-epic work.
tickets.title: Define full FWG AI gameplay and authority contract

acceptanceCriteria.text: Record a runnable LittleBit proof and actual peak memory, or an explicit blocker; ordinary GGUF/GPTQ/AWQ is not a substitute.

Define at least three feasible tool-capable parent candidates using official model cards, licenses and current architecture support. Record exact revisions/chat templates and required training resources.
Pin LittleBit versus opt-in LittleBit-2 settings and preserve tokenizer/tool formatting; no claim that parameter BPW equals whole runtime memory.

tickets.body: Inventory CPU/GPU/VRAM/RAM and available storage, with Bannerlord headroom. Pin official SamsungLabs/LittleBit revision, supported architectures, training dependencies and inference path. Verify actual factorized checkpoint loading/generation on a feasible small checkpoint before scheduling large compression. Separate training resources from local inference resources; any external compute spend needs its own authorization.
tickets.title: Establish LittleBit and target-hardware feasibility

acceptanceCriteria.text: Elf/dwarf/tidekin fixtures remain FWG identities despite base-culture art mappings; magic-off and unknown capabilities are explicit.
Live ownership, location, diplomacy and alive state override genesis records; world A/B and same-world separate-campaign queries do not leak.
Context retrieval has deterministic token limits and tests for missing entities, long histories and contradictory/stale facts.

tickets.body: Project verified WorldDataBundle, CompiledWorldDataset and live TaleWorlds state into a versioned read-only fact API. Preserve civilization/cultureUid separately from presentation Culture; use world instance/content identity. Include peoples, generated rulers/settlements/history, geography/travel, magic availability and current mutation state. Bound retrieval and identify provenance/freshness.
tickets.title: Expose versioned FWG facts and live campaign context

acceptanceCriteria.text: Malformed/unknown tools, foreign IDs, invalid amounts, stale state, replayed requests and injected lore cannot commit side effects.
Multi-step plans revalidate each step and expose partial completion; failed steps do not fabricate success or replay completed effects.
Automated tests verify exact effects and error paths using independent expected state, plus one real game-thread action probe.

tickets.body: Create schema-versioned query/action contracts and capability registry. Validate entity scope, actor authority, resources, current-state revision, magic rules, bounded arguments and idempotency before game-thread commit. Track proposed, validated, queued, committed, failed and cancelled states; return structured results. Treat dialogue and retrieved lore as data.
tickets.title: Implement typed tool proposals and validated game-thread execution

acceptanceCriteria.text: Protocol tests cover streaming/partial JSON, invalid tool output, refusal, disconnect, overload, cancellation and late replies.
Campaign stays playable when provider is absent; no silent cloud fallback or fake successful dialogue/actions.
One genuine local completion uses the production transport and negotiated tool format; later LittleBit serving can plug into the same contract.

tickets.body: Implement provider-independent messages/tools and a local endpoint adapter. Bound queues, response length, context, retries and per-NPC budgets. Cancel on scene/campaign unload, timeout and superseding requests; inference never blocks the game thread. Record model/runtime identity and request timings without secrets.
tickets.title: Build asynchronous local inference transport and request lifecycle

acceptanceCriteria.text: Two NPCs with different knowledge answer differently without privileged secrets leaking; rumours remain beliefs until corroborated.
Summaries retain commitments, provenance and contradictions under context limits; death/ownership changes invalidate stale assumptions.
Same-world two-campaign and A→B→A tests show no shared memory or cache leakage.

tickets.body: Build bounded memories and separate authoritative facts, witnessed events, hearsay and disputed claims. Define forgetting/summarization, trust and knowledge access; keep NPC personality/backstory grounded in FWG sources. Persist identifiers using campaign instance + world content + entity ID.
tickets.title: Implement campaign-bound NPC memory, beliefs and knowledge propagation

acceptanceCriteria.text: Player can converse with generated characters and follow a query→tool→answer chain grounded in real state.
Rejected or pending actions are represented honestly; cancelling or closing dialogue drops stale replies safely.
Offline/local-provider failure still permits normal campaign interaction and a clear retry path.

tickets.body: Implement conversation entry/exit, character context, visible waiting/cancel/failure states and a player-readable event/commitment history. Display actual action outcomes; support follow-up turns using tool results and current facts. UI must not expose irrelevant implementation details.
tickets.title: Connect grounded dialogue and tool results to player UI

acceptanceCriteria.text: Two playable intrigue scenarios span multiple NPCs and turns, with observable belief/relation and political outcomes.
Expose discovery, betrayal, refusal, interruption and conflicting-loyalty branches; unavailable world features are not invented.
Player and NPCs can dispute false claims; secrets reveal only through explicit knowledge rules.

tickets.body: Build schemes as persisted multi-step plans with actors, target, evidence/rumour provenance, resources, secrecy, commitments and success/failure states. Initial scenarios include a false accusation challenged by evidence and a negotiated defection or alliance affected by trust. Use validated political tools for material consequences; NPC dialogue alone cannot alter facts.
tickets.title: Implement political intrigue with beliefs, commitments and consequences

acceptanceCriteria.text: Generated kingdoms/clans can negotiate and perform war/peace, clan transition, fief transfer and a payable agreement in owned test campaigns.
Invalid authority, destroyed factions, stale ownership, insufficient funds and duplicate payments reject safely with auditable outcomes.
Each adapter has source/API evidence, independent state assertions, and current-version in-game proof rather than only mocked calls.

tickets.body: Independently implement the observed political seams: relations; war/peace; alliances/trade commitments; clan joining/leaving; fief ownership; gold, tribute and reparations. Use version-pinned public APIs where possible, with explicit actor/ownership/resource validation. Preserve ongoing agreements and partial payment semantics.
tickets.title: Implement Bannerlord political and economic action adapters

acceptanceCriteria.text: Tests and in-game probes cover native war/peace proposals, AI proposals, nested actions and re-entry without duplicate consequences.
Feature disabled, provider unavailable, new game, load and teardown retain the declared ownership/fallback behavior.
Patch targets are pinned and missing/changed targets fail visibly without silently disabling all politics.

tickets.body: Study AI Influence suppression/WithBypass pattern, then design scoped MNBL ownership so native and AI decisions do not double-apply or cancel each other. Verify compatibility with generated campaign behaviors and War Sails. Avoid global suppression before AI is ready; restore expected behavior on disable/failure.
tickets.title: Resolve AI versus vanilla political simulation ownership

acceptanceCriteria.text: A negotiated quest executes across generated locations and completes only on verified conditions, with reward issued once.
Unreachable land/sea routes, changed target ownership, dead actors and interrupted chains produce explicit replanning/failure.
An in-game route includes relevant periodic/sea behavior when enabled and persists after save/load.

tickets.body: Expose routes and party/settlement targets from the current FWG world. Implement movement/order chains and quests with verifiable objectives, cancellation, deadlines and material rewards. Respect wrap navigation and land/sea capability; avoid arbitrary teleport or invented targets.
tickets.title: Implement generated-world travel, practical orders and grounded quests

acceptanceCriteria.text: An allowed AI-requested magic event changes the real generated world and subsequent AI context observes its committed state.
Magic-off, hidden school, invalid/foreign settlement, invalid strength, unavailable producer and insufficient gameplay authority fail without changes.
In-flight mutation cancellation, failure and duplicate request paths are verified; save/load preserves the actual mutation and its narrative consequence.

tickets.body: Expose an explicit adapter to internal WorldMutations.Report(MagicEvent), retaining visible-school/settlement/strength validation, producer identity, asynchronous work and map-safe-point application. Add gameplay authority/cost/cooldown rules in MNBL. This existing API is a settlement magic event, not a general terrain editor; additional advertised effects require implemented contracts.
tickets.title: Bridge AI fantasy actions into real FWG mutation

acceptanceCriteria.text: A generated-world event changes relevant NPC priorities and triggers a bounded observable plan without forcing every NPC to infer every tick.
Queue overload, event cascades, repeated failures and time acceleration stay within the contract budgets.
Unsupported fantasy effects remain unavailable, while implemented magic/political effects update both world facts and NPC beliefs.

tickets.body: Schedule NPC decisions and event responses using current campaign facts and knowledge propagation. Bound active plans, calls and event cascades; use campaign time for expiry and deterministic rules for which NPCs get attention. NPC actions use the same validated tools as player-mediated conversations.
tickets.title: Schedule NPC initiative and world events within simulation budgets

acceptanceCriteria.text: Cold restart and rollback restore memory and material state consistently; no future-memory contamination, duplicate payments or repeated magic effects.
A/B worlds, two campaigns from one world, same campaign older save, corrupt AI data and version mismatch each have explicit tested behavior.
Existing pre-AI saves and AI-disabled play follow documented compatibility paths; teardown releases all campaign references.

tickets.body: Integrate versioned AI persistence into existing campaign save binding. Include committed action journal, pending plans, agreement state, knowledge and prompt/schema/config identity. Define save-slot rollback semantics and atomicity across inference and world mutation. Cancel pending work on load and rebuild from saved state.
tickets.title: Make memory, plans and world actions save-consistent

acceptanceCriteria.text: Both slices visibly affect generated campaign state and survive a cold save/load; no fixed Calradia targets are required.
Adversarial and failure matrix includes secret leakage, fabricated IDs, stale replies, denied actions, model outage and interrupted mutations.
Evidence names exact builds/worlds and known limitations; unresolved required behavior blocks sprint acceptance.

tickets.body: Run owned test campaigns covering dialogue→knowledge→intrigue→political consequence and dialogue→quest/travel→magic→world response. Capture input, tool requests/results, state assertions, save identity and package hash. Test failures as well as successes.
tickets.title: Verify full FWG interaction vertical slices

acceptanceCriteria.text: At least 100 held-out scenarios across the declared capability/failure categories use frozen prompts, tool schemas, expected state and scoring rules.
Score tool selection, schema and argument validity, grounded entity targeting, multi-step completion, refusal/abstention, knowledge leakage and actual effects separately.
Freeze numerical pass thresholds and latency/RAM/VRAM budgets before candidate results; critical invalid state mutations or cross-campaign leaks are hard failures.

tickets.body: Create versioned scenario fixtures and deterministic action-state oracles covering all implemented capabilities. Split training/calibration/dev/held-out sets before compression and keep held-out cases out of prompt tuning/QAT. Include ambiguous queries, no-tool turns, dependent/parallel calls where supported, invalid authority, schema errors, tool failure/recovery, multi-turn intrigue, unknown lore and magic-off.
tickets.title: Freeze held-out FWG tool-use evaluation suite

acceptanceCriteria.text: Publish per-scenario raw results and aggregate uncertainty/repeated-run results, not only a leaderboard average.
Select at least two eligible parents by actual FWG tool-task performance and local-compression feasibility; infeasible models have measured or sourced exclusion reasons.
Separate unconstrained model reliability from schema-constrained serving gains; use matched settings in paired comparisons.

tickets.body: Run at least three feasible instruction/tool-capable parent checkpoints through the production protocol. Record model revisions, tokenizer/chat templates, reasoning settings, context lengths, decoding seeds, runtime and hardware. Candidate discovery uses current official sources; model-family support alone is not proof of tool capability.
tickets.title: Rank tool-capable parent models on the same FWG tasks

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each derivative loads and generates locally with actual LittleBit factorized layers; report serialized size, actual tensor storage and effective compression.
Paired parent/compressed evaluations measure tool-task degradation and critical failures using identical held-out scenarios and matched decoding.
Record all failed configurations and recovery/tuning attempts; do not select by perplexity alone or replace LittleBit with conventional quantization.

tickets.body: Compress at least two selected parents using pinned SamsungLabs LittleBit and at least two effective-bit settings each, including a less aggressive reference. Record QAT/calibration data, seeds, training resources, recipe, checkpoint hashes and failures. Preserve tool-use/chat formatting and keep held-out suite excluded. LittleBit-2 may be an explicit ablation, not an undisclosed substitute.
tickets.title: Produce and evaluate genuine LittleBit model derivatives

acceptanceCriteria.text: The production campaign completes real tool cycles against at least two compressed candidates with no remote inference substitution.
Measure time to first token, end-to-end p50/p95, throughput, peak RAM/VRAM and game-frame impact at the frozen concurrency/context levels.
Cancellation, restart, OOM, timeout and malformed responses are exercised without corrupting the campaign.

tickets.body: Serve real compressed checkpoints through the production local adapter. Validate tool templates/parsing, context/KV memory, concurrency and cold/warm latency with Bannerlord running. If generic inference servers do not support factorized layers, implement and verify a dedicated local service rather than claiming support.
tickets.title: Integrate the selected LittleBit runtime with live Bannerlord

acceptanceCriteria.text: Decision includes parent/derivative identifiers, compression recipe, per-category scores, confidence/repeated-run summary, resource measurements and exact reproduction commands.
Selected checkpoint passes the frozen correctness/resource gates and final gameplay/save-load checks; all required failures are resolved.
If no compressed model passes, record no-go and leave final acceptance unpassed; do not claim a successful local model on unrun or synthetic results.

tickets.body: Aggregate quality/size/latency evidence and select the strongest reliable tool model that meets the frozen local deployment budgets after LittleBit compression. Rerun the full live campaign slices with the selected checkpoint and save/load. Document a reproducible setup and honest no-go outcome when no candidate qualifies.
tickets.title: Publish paired evaluation results and final model decision
